title: Separated frequency blocks do not disturb earlier partial sum maxima
statement: For an analytic polynomial P supported in [0,d], Q=e_m P is supported in [m,m+d] and A_{m+r}Q=e_m A_r P. If earlier polynomials have degree <m, Q does not alter their earlier partial sums. The design additionally demands that frequency translation make completed Q uniformly small on earlier good sets.
proof_plan: The frequency support and partial-sum identity follow coefficient by coefficient, with m larger than all earlier degrees. The additional design clause is NOT established: |e_m P|=|P| for every m, so translation cannot reduce completed magnitude. Proposed repair keeps the useful separation identity and obtains completed-block control independently from amplitude scaling plus summability of integrals (or Markov with explicitly budgeted exceptional sets). Owner must reconcile the false clause; do not certify the stated full design claim.

references.title: Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, third edition

unresolved_obligations: Mathematical escalation: the magnitude-smallness clause attributed to frequency translation is false without an independent smallness hypothesis. P=1 witnesses that no shift makes it <1/2 on a nonempty set.
